chapter: Learning the trombone and jam sessions
title: Band instruction at school under John Scott
summary: They played marches and overtures, jazzed things up, and were taught by John Scott, a clarinetist.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: But you got instruction, formal music instruction at that school or did you just play with --

You play marches (unintelligible). We used to jazz up the marches sometime. They'd get after us and tell us to tone it down. We'd try to put some jazz notes in the marches. But we'd play a few overtures, things like the William Tell Overture, a few things. But mostly it was march. It was march music. When we were on our own, we'd try anything with those instruments, you know.

Just experimenting around, of course. The guy who taught us, his name was John Scott. And he was from Richmond, Virginia. Big, tall, nice looking brown-skinned guy. And he was the teacher, but he taught all the instruments. And he really didn't know all the instruments that well but he taught us to the best of his ability. His instrument, I think, was clarinet. Naturally the clarinet players got a better musical education than the rest of us did. But we had a lot of fun playing.

We'd just get together and anything we heard we try to play it. March, or any kind of thing, you know. If we heard an operatic singer we'd try to play what they were singing. It was just a challenge to us to play things, you know. Half of us didn't -- never knew what key we were in. We were just fooling around.
